what_its_for: Disopyramide is used to treat certain types of irregular heartbeats (called arrhythmias). It helps your heart beat in a more normal, steady rhythm by slowing certain electrical signals in the heart.
how_to_take: Take disopyramide exactly as your doctor prescribes. Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. The extended-release capsules (Norpace CR) should NOT be crushed, chewed, or opened — swallow them whole. You may take this medicine with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. Take it at evenly spaced times throughout the day to keep a steady level in your body.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 400 to 800 mg per day, divided into doses taken every 6 hours (regular capsules) or every 12 hours (extended-release capsules). Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight, kidney function, and how your heart responds. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if it is more than 4 hours until your next scheduled dose (for regular capsules) or more than 6 hours (for extended-release capsules). If it is too close to your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. NEVER take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store disopyramide at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can lower your blood sugar and increase dizziness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this drug affects you, since it can cause blurred vision or dizziness. Avoid getting overheated or dehydrated (drink enough fluids). Tell your doctor or pharmacist before taking any new medicines — including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements — because many medicines can interact with disopyramide. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice unless your doctor says it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a fast, slow, or very irregular heartbeat; chest pain or tightness; shortness of breath or difficulty breathing; severe dizziness or fainting; swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles; signs of low blood sugar such as sudden sweating, shakiness, confusion, or feeling very hungry; difficulty urinating or no urination; blurred vision or eye pain; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Disopyramide begins working within 30 minutes to 3 hours after you take a dose. However, it may take several days of consistent use before your heart rhythm is fully controlled. Keep taking it even if you feel well — do not stop suddenly without talking to your doctor, as stopping abruptly can cause dangerous changes in your heart rhythm.
special_populations: Older adults (65+): You may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, dry mouth, and urinary problems. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Kidney or liver problems: Your dose may need to be reduced because the drug is cleared more slowly from your body. Pregnancy: This medicine may cause harm to an unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Disopyramide passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Dosing in children is based on body weight and must be carefully managed by a doctor.
